$doc: Policy read by scripts/gate_workflow_drift.py / workflow-templates/gate-workflow-drift.yml. Converts governance-sync.yml's old advisory ::warning:: on workflow drift into a REQUIRED-check ratchet. See governance/workflow-template-containment.md for the full design and its justification.
unit: baseline-version releases — each commit in FuzeSDLC that bumped governance/baseline-version.txt (governance/versioning.md §5), counted between the commit a repo's stamped digest last matched and the commit its baselineRef currently resolves to.
why_not_any_drift: governance-sync.yml cannot push .github/workflows/** for any repo today — the default GITHUB_TOKEN is blocked by GitHub's `workflows` OAuth scope, and the workflows-scoped fuze-agent App token that would let it self-heal has never been granted that permission (governance/file-ownership.md). Failing on the FIRST digest mismatch would therefore turn every onboarded repo red on the very next canonical release, for a condition none of them can fix from inside their own CI — the exact alarm-fatigue failure this fleet has removed from gate-lint/gate-test/gate-dependency-scan elsewhere (required-checks.json). Repos need a real chance to catch up via a human bootstrap re-run or the nightly sweep before this becomes blocking.
why_not_purely_advisory: an advisory warning nobody is forced to act on is functionally the same as no gate — the failure this whole file exists to fix. A ratchet with a bounded grace window keeps both properties: real drift becomes genuinely blocking, but only after it has survived enough releases that failing to act on it is a process gap, not bad luck.
why_three: three releases gives the nightly governance-reconciliation sweep and a manual scripts/sdlc-bootstrap.sh re-run multiple independent chances to close the gap before it blocks a merge, while still bounding how long a real drift can hide — tune down once the workflows-scoped App token is actually granted (file-ownership.md) and reconciliation can self-heal same-day.
unknown_provenance: advisory only, NEVER hard-fails. A stamped digest that cannot be matched to any commit in the canonical template's own tracked history (a renamed/retired template, an incomplete or shallow canonical checkout, or a marker older than this gate) is ambiguous, not proven drift — failing on an unprovable signal is the same false-positive shape file-ownership.md and required-checks.json already warn against ('a check whose output carried no information while looking like it did').
never_examined: files with no `fuze:managed` marker (detached, or a repo's own workflow that happens to share a canonical template's name) and files that do not exist yet in .github/workflows/** — both are supported, non-drift states handled by governance_sync.py, not this gate.
